name: ESP32 DevKit board (ESP32-WROOM-32, 30-pin)
ram: 520KB SRAM (about 320KB actually available to your program)

button.note: The BOOT button is on GPIO0 and reads LOW when pressed. After boot you can use it as an ordinary button (pinMode(0, INPUT_PULLUP)). The other button, EN, is reset

buses.i2c: Default SDA GPIO21 / SCL GPIO22 (Wire.begin() with no arguments uses this pair; you can also pick any pins with Wire.begin(sda, scl))
buses.spi: VSPI (the default SPI): SCK 18 / MISO 19 / MOSI 23 / CS 5; HSPI: SCK 14 / MISO 12 / MOSI 13 / CS 15
buses.uart: Serial (UART0): TX GPIO1 / RX GPIO3, wired to the onboard USB-serial chip, so you see output as soon as you plug in USB; Serial2 (UART2): TX 17 / RX 16 for external modules; Serial1's default pins are taken by the Flash, so to use it call Serial1.begin(115200, SERIAL_8N1, rx, tx) with your own pins

pwm_pins: Any output-capable GPIO can analogWrite (the internal LEDC has 16 channels)
34, 35, 36 and 39 are input-only and cannot do PWM
power: 3.3V logic, and the I/O is NOT 5V-tolerant! Signal lines from 5V sensors need a voltage divider or a level shifter. The VIN header pin is USB 5V straight in (you can also feed the board 5V here); the 3V3 pin comes from the onboard AMS1117 regulator and can supply roughly 300-500mA (verify). Wi-Fi transmit bursts can draw up to 500mA, so a poor USB cable causes mysterious resets
flash_how: The board has a built-in USB-serial chip (CP2102 or CH340). Plug a micro-USB cable into your computer and run pio run -t upload; it enters download mode automatically. Windows and older macOS may need the CP210x or CH340 driver. If it hangs at Connecting........_____, hold the BOOT button for 2 seconds while it prints the dots, then release (some boards need this every time; a 10uF capacitor between EN and GND fixes it). Add upload_speed = 921600 to platformio.ini for much faster uploads. Serial: pio device monitor at 115200 baud
gotchas: The I/O is not 5V-tolerant. This is the most common mistake when coming from the UNO: a 5V module's output signal cannot connect directly to the ESP32

There are many board variants (30-pin DOIT V1, 38-pin DevKitC, etc.) with slightly different header layouts, but the GPIO numbers are universal; read the numbers printed on the board (verify against the board in your hand)
GPIO34, 35, 36 and 39 are input-only with no internal pull-up; add an external pull-up resistor for buttons
ADC2 channels (GPIO0, 2, 4, 12-15, 25-27) can't be read while Wi-Fi is on. For Wi-Fi plus analog, use the ADC1 pins: 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 39
The ADC is 12-bit (0-4095) but nonlinear and clipped at the top; readings near 3.3V are inaccurate. Don't rely on it where precision matters

Strapping (boot) pins: GPIO0 (LOW while pressing BOOT enters download mode), GPIO2, GPIO5, GPIO12, GPIO15. If a peripheral pulls these to the wrong level at power-up, boot fails; GPIO12 in particular must not be HIGH at power-up
GPIO6-11 connect to the internal Flash. 30-pin boards simply don't expose them; 38-pin boards do, but never use them
analogWrite works directly on ESP32 Arduino 2.x/3.x; the ledcSetup/ledcAttachPin calls in older tutorials are the low-level way, replaced by ledcAttach in 3.x
Serial is UART0 over USB. Don't use GPIO1/GPIO3 as ordinary I/O or serial output breaks
Most versions have the onboard LED on GPIO2, but some boards have no onboard LED (other than the power LED); don't assume your program isn't running
HardwareTimer, IWatchdog and friends are STM32duino-only APIs and don't exist on ESP32; the ESP32 uses its own timerBegin / esp_task_wdt
The board is wide and covers every hole on both sides of a breadboard; buy a large breadboard or join two together

left.name: EN
left.note: Pull LOW to reset; in parallel with the EN button

left.name: VP / GPIO36
left.note: Input only, no pull-up. ADC works even with Wi-Fi on

left.name: D32 / GPIO32
left.note: First choice for reading a potentiometer (unaffected by Wi-Fi)

left.name: D25 / GPIO25
left.note: A true analog output (DAC); can produce sound

left.name: D14 / GPIO14
left.note: Outputs a short PWM burst at power-up

left.name: D12 / GPIO12
left.note: Strapping pin: must be LOW at power-up or boot fails. Don't add a pull-up

left.name: VIN
left.note: USB 5V straight out; you can also feed the board 5V here. Power 5V modules from this pin

right.name: D22 / GPIO22
right.note: Default I2C SCL; the OLED goes here

right.name: TX0 / GPIO1
right.note: Wired to the USB-serial chip; don't use as I/O

right.name: RX0 / GPIO3
right.note: Wired to the USB-serial chip; don't use as I/O

right.name: D21 / GPIO21
right.note: Default I2C SDA; the OLED goes here

right.name: D5 / GPIO5
right.note: Default SPI chip select. Strapping pin; outputs a short PWM burst at power-up

right.name: TX2 / GPIO17
right.note: Serial2; connect to a Bluetooth/GPS module's RX

right.name: RX2 / GPIO16
right.note: Serial2; connect to the module's TX

right.name: D2 / GPIO2
right.note: Onboard blue LED, active-high. Also a strapping pin; must be LOW or floating while downloading

right.name: D15 / GPIO15
right.note: Strapping pin: LOW at power-up silences the boot log

right.name: 3V3
right.note: Onboard LDO output; powers sensors and the OLED

pin_map.note: Recipes and snippets are written for the Blue Pill; translate pins with this table (left = Blue Pill, right = this board GPIO)
